enonce_intro_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_12_fig_1.png)

Figure 4 shows a sector of a circle of radius $10\,\text{cm}$. Given that the length $PQ$ is $12\,\text{cm}$ and the area of the sector is $64.4\,\text{cm}^2$.

figures.legende: Figure 4: sector OPQ of a circle of radius 10 cm, centre O; chord PQ = 12 cm with R the foot of the perpendicular from O; the segment between the chord PQ and the arc is shaded.

incertitudes: Q12 : O est le centre du cercle et R le pied de la perpendiculaire à PQ (angle droit marqué sur la figure). L'aire de la région ombrée (segment) = aire du secteur donnée (64,4) moins l'aire du triangle OPQ = 16,4 cm2 ; avec l'aire exacte du secteur (64,35) on trouve 16,35, soit 16,4 aussi.

questions.corrige_markdown:
$OR$ is perpendicular to the chord $PQ$ and passes through the centre $O$, so $R$ is the midpoint of $PQ$.

$RQ=\dfrac{PQ}{2}=\dfrac{12}{2}=6$ cm.

**$RQ=6$ cm.**

Triangle $ORQ$ is right-angled at $R$ with hypotenuse $OQ=10$ cm (the radius) and $RQ=6$ cm.

By Pythagoras: $OR^2=OQ^2-RQ^2=10^2-6^2=100-36=64$.

$OR=\sqrt{64}=8$ cm.

**$OR=8$ cm.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) area of the shaded region. *[7 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The shaded region (a segment) is the sector $OPQ$ minus the triangle $OPQ$.

Area of triangle $OPQ=\dfrac12\times PQ\times OR=\dfrac12\times12\times8=48$ cm$^2$.

Area of shaded region $=64.4-48=16.4$ cm$^2$.

(Check: $\angle POQ=2\sin^{-1}(0.6)\approx73.74^\circ$, so the sector area is $\dfrac{73.74}{360}\times\pi\times10^2\approx64.35$ cm$^2$, which agrees with the given $64.4$.)

**Area of the shaded region $=16.4$ cm$^2$.**
